headline: Stuut, a New York company whose AI software chases and matches customer payments, has raised $52.5 million.
score_reason: Kept at pool score 5: a mid-sized round with company-supplied figures.
importance_line: What changed is that AI agents now do most of the chasing and matching of payments at some large companies, which matters to the finance workers who did that work, then to businesses buying such tools, and the doubt is that the automation rates and customer count come from Stuut itself.
summary: The AI Insider reports that Stuut's Series B round (a mid-stage investment round) was led by Insight Partners, with Andreessen Horowitz, M12, Microsoft's Venture Fund and Activant taking part, and will help it expand into credit, lending and funds movement. Stuut, which automates the process from invoice to cash received (order-to-cash), says 81.7% of its outbound collections work now runs without human involvement and that it has more than 150 customers, including Honeywell, ZoomInfo and Verifone.
